name: IPinfo Inc.

hosts.note: Base URL of the current API (IPinfo Lite /lite and Core/Plus /lookup endpoints, and /batch), per the IPinfo developer documentation.
Documented IPv4-only variant of the API host.
Documented IPv6-only variant of the API host.

The developer documentation names ipinfo.io as the legacy API service (for example https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8?token=..., and the legacy batch endpoint https://ipinfo.io/batch), which it describes as actively maintained. The same host also serves IPinfo's website, so a link to a documentation page also matches.
IPv6 variant of the legacy API host, named in the developer documentation.

jurisdictions.note: The DPA names the data importer as IPinfo Inc., 300 Lenora Street #516, Seattle, WA 98121, USA, in the role of processor. The privacy policy states that the Services 'are hosted in the United States', and the DPA states that IPinfo 'is a recipient of European Data in the United States'. Annex 2 of the DPA states that the services are hosted on Google Cloud; Annex 3 lists Google LLC/Google Cloud for data storage with country US. The Terms of Service select the laws of the State of Washington.

euRegion.notes: No EU hosting or data residency option was found on the developer documentation, privacy policy, Terms of Service or DPA read for this entry. Every sub-processor listed in Annex 3 of the DPA on the access date carries the country US.

dataCategories.note: The API's input is an IP address, and a request for /me looks up the caller's own address. The DPA defines Customer Data as 'any data, including IP addresses, that you or your end users submit to the Service (including through API requests)', and states that the parties agree to handle IP addresses under the DPA.

notes: Contracting entity: IPinfo Inc., Seattle, Washington. The DPA forms part of the Terms of Service, applies to every account, free or paid, and is accepted by accepting the Agreement or using the Service; a signed copy is available on request. Transfers: the DPA incorporates the 2021 EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two where the customer is a controller, Module Three where it is a processor), governed by Irish law, with the UK Addendum and Swiss modifications. DPF: none of the privacy policy, Terms of Service or DPA mentions the Data Privacy Framework, and a search of the participant list for 'IPinfo', 'ipinfo' and 'IP Info' returned no record, active or inactive, so no DPF mechanism is recorded. The list renders client-side and was queried through the JSON API its own bundle calls (POST https://dpfapi.azurewebsites.net/api/participants, Status Active and Inactive); the same query returned Stripe, LLC as a control. Sub-processors: Annex 3 of the DPA on the access date listed eleven, all with country US: Google LLC/Google Cloud (data storage), Stripe, Amplitude, Salesforce, Cloudflare (CDN, storage and distribution of data files), HubSpot, Mailgun, PostHog, Retool, Slack and Zendesk. The DPA commits to 30 days' notice of a new sub-processor by updating Annex 3, and to email notice for customers who subscribe. Packages: node-ipinfo and the PyPI package ipinfo are linked from IPinfo's libraries page and their registry metadata point to the ipinfo GitHub organisation. The npm package named ipinfo is published by an individual (repository github.com/IonicaBizau/node-ipinfo), not by IPinfo, and is recorded as a wrapper. Separately from the API, the privacy policy describes an IPinfo SDK distributed in third-party mobile applications and IPinfo's own apps that collect device location and Wi-Fi data; that collection is not part of an API call and is not modelled here.
